paper.title: Do tax incentives for saving in pension accounts cause debt accumulation? Evidence from Danish register data
paper.code_data_availability: 'Supplementary material associated with this article can be found, in the online version, at doi: …

variables_mentioned: years since last change of address

registers.name_in_paper: Danish tax authorities (third-party reported annual information from banks and mortgage institutions)

registers.role: outcomes (mortgage repayments) and mortgage loan characteristics
variables_mentioned: mortgage institutions' assessment of property values

registers.name_in_paper: Danmarks Nationalbank and Danish Insurance Association (aggregate series, Fig. 1)
registers.role: descriptive aggregate time series (total household debt and total pension contributions)
variables_mentioned: outstanding debt in households (banks and mortgage institutions)

registers.name_in_paper: Google Trends (Fig. B1) and Infomedia newspaper archive (Fig. B2)
registers.role: descriptive evidence that the public was aware of the rule change

linkages: Panel data from Statistics Denmark and the Danish mortgage institutions are merged using anonymised personal identifiers that cover everyone residing in Denmark.
Individual saving and debt information is reported each year by third parties, i.e. banks and mortgage institutions, to the Danish tax authorities.

sample.universe: Everyone residing in Denmark covered by the merged Statistics Denmark and mortgage institution panel data, 2003-2013
sample.unit_of_observation: individual-year (person-year); Table A5 uses a cross-section of 2008 values
selection_rules: individuals with annuity pension contributions of DKK 80,000-150,000 in 2008 (two years prior to implementation, one year prior to announcement)
individuals with DKK 100,001-150,000 assigned to treatment, those with DKK 80,000-100,000 assigned as non-treated
self-employed individuals including spouse excluded (they were not fully subject to the changed tax rules)
individuals aged 60 or above excluded (eligible for early retirement schemes)
people not fully liable to taxation in Denmark excluded
changes in non-retirement saving and debt accounts censored at the 1st and 99th percentile
sample.n_observations: 599,744 (unbalanced panel; Table 1 note states 599,744 while Table 3 and Table A1-A2 state 599,774)

construction_notes: flow variables are calculated as year-on-year changes in stock variables, so annual variations in price and quantity measures cannot be separated

retirement savings are measured before taxes and non-retirement savings after taxes; pension contributions are converted with a mean tax rate tau_i = total taxes paid / taxable income, fixed at its 2008 level, as P_i,t(1 - tau_i)

control vector X_i,t-2 is lagged two years and contains income, age, work tenure, marital status, a dummy for being divorced within 1 year, a dummy for being divorced within 2 years, years since individual i last changed address and housing wealth
educational level is measured prior to the reform announcement as discrete values 1-6 (primary and secondary school, vocational training, short, medium and higher education)
medium and top tax bracket dummies take the value 1 for individuals whose pre-reform taxable income corresponded to not paying medium and top taxes, each interacted with year dummies
the donut-hole robustness test excludes individuals with 2008 annuity pension contributions of DKK 90,000-110,000
loan-to-value is outstanding mortgage debt divided by the mortgage institutions' assessment of property values; loan-to-income is outstanding debt as a share of annual income
normalised by last year's income, the mean savings rate in the estimation sample is 8.5 percent in 2009 with a standard deviation of 39.6 percent

claims.statement: A DKK 1 reduction in annuity pension contributions caused by the Danish 2010 cap on tax-deductible annuity pension contributions changes annual life-long pensions by DKK 0.567.

treatment.label: Reduction in annual annuity pension contributions (per DKK 1)

register_source.value: Danish tax authorities' third-party reported annual information, merged at Statistics Denmark; no DST register code is named in the paper.

definition.value: A 1 unit (DKK 1) reduction in annual individual contributions to annuity pension schemes, P_i,t, induced by the Danish 2010 tax reform that capped the tax deduction for annuity pension contributions at DKK 100,000. In Eqs. (2) and (3) annuity pension contributions are instrumented by Treat_i x Post_i,t; in Eq. (3) they enter after taxes as P_i,t(1-tau_i) with the mean tax rate tau_i fixed at its 2008 level. Table 1 prints the change in each alternative account per 1 unit REDUCTION in annuity pension contributions, so a positive printed value means the account grows when annuity contributions fall.

timing.value: Measured annually; the reform was implemented in 2010 and Post_i,t equals 1 in all years after implementation.

register_source.value: Danish tax authorities' third-party reported annual information, merged at Statistics Denmark; no DST register code is named in the paper.

definition.value: Annual individual contributions to life-long pension schemes (paid out in annuities until the owner dies and taxed as regular income), in DKK, measured before taxes; the dependent variable Z_i,t of Eq. (2).

timing.value: Annual flow, measured over the post-reform years (Post_i,t = 1 in all years after implementation of the reform in 2010); the panel runs 2003-2013 and mortgage information 2009-2013.

units.value: DKK change in the outcome account per DKK 1 reduction in annuity pension contributions (the paper reports it in cents per DKK)

magnitude.interpretation: almost 57 cents is shifted to life-long pension accounts

estimand.target_population: Treated individuals (2008 annuity pension contributions of DKK 100,001-150,000) who changed their annuity pension contributions because of the reform.
estimand.compliers: Savers who reduced annuity pension contributions in response to the DKK 100,000 deduction ceiling; the paper estimates that about 23 percent of individuals actively rebalanced their savings.
estimand.time_horizon: All post-reform years: Post_i,t takes the value 1 in all years after implementation of the reform (2010-2013).

population.description: Individuals residing in Denmark with annuity pension contributions of DKK 80,000-150,000 in 2008; self-employed individuals and their spouses excluded, individuals aged 60 or above excluded, and people not fully liable to taxation in Denmark excluded. 56,372 individuals, 599,744 person-year observations, 2003-2013.
population.ages: below 60 (individuals aged 60 or above are excluded); estimation-sample mean age 43.3
subgroups_defined: treated: annuity pension contributions of DKK 100,001-150,000 in 2008
non-treated: annuity pension contributions of DKK 80,000-100,000 in 2008
population.selection: Groups are assigned on 2008 annuity pension contributions, one year prior to the reform announcement; the estimation sample is explicitly not representative of the full Danish population and covers savers in the upper part of the income distribution (estimation-sample mean gross income DKK 668,500 against DKK 305,200 in the full sample).

identification.source_of_variation: The Danish 2010 tax reform, which made employer-paid plus individual contributions to annuity pension schemes tax-deductible only up to DKK 100,000; individuals with 2008 annuity contributions above the threshold are treated, those below are non-treated.

key_assumptions.assumption: Parallel pre-trends: the treated and non-treated groups would have had similar changes in the savings outcome had the reform not been implemented.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Graphical inspection of pre-reform group means in Figs. 3, 4a, 4b, B3 and B4

key_assumptions.assumption: Instrument relevance: Treat_i x Post_i,t is strongly correlated with annuity pension contributions.
key_assumptions.supported_by: First stage in Table 2 column 1: a DKK 21,038 reduction in annuity pension contributions, statistically significant with p < .001

key_assumptions.assumption: Exclusion restriction: Treat_i x Post_i,t affects the savings outcome only through annuity pension contributions and is not correlated with some common third factor.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Graphical inspection of pre-trends in the outcome variables

key_assumptions.assumption: No anticipation: individuals did not adjust annuity pension contributions before the reform was implemented.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Fig. 2: the pre-reform histogram of annuity pension contributions is smooth around the DKK 100,000-threshold, while bunching appears only after implementation

implies_edges.to: annuity pension contributions in pre-reform years

key_assumptions.assumption: No self-selection into treatment: groups are assigned on 2008 annuity pension contributions, one year before the reform was announced.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Timing of the assignment rule

key_assumptions.assumption: No mean reversion: the measured reduction in annuity pension contributions is not a mechanical consequence of assigning groups on a single year's contributions.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Placebo reforms in 2008, 2007, 2006 and 2005 (Table 2) and the donut-hole test

key_assumptions.assumption: Inherent savings propensities are approximately constant over the observation period.
The price (substitution) channel dominates the wealth channel, so the comparison of treated and non-treated savers recovers the substitution effect.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Cites Duflo et al. (2006) and Engelhardt and Kumar (2007)

key_assumptions.assumption: Monotonicity of the response to the instrument, required for the 2SLS estimate to be a local average treatment effect.

threats_discussed: mean reversion in annuity pension contributions (tested with placebo reforms, Table 2)
sensitivity to the assignment window around the DKK 100,000-threshold (Fig. 5)
misallocation into the control group of individuals who behave like treated individuals (Table A2)
individuals forced to move out of their homes after 2010 (non-mover subsample, Table A4 column 1)
differential housing wealth and income trends between the groups (Figs. B4a and B4b)
differential exposure to unemployment and labour supply responses (Figs. B5a and B5b)
other elements of the 2010 tax reform: removal of the middle tax bracket and increase of the top tax bracket (Table 1 columns 3-4)
serial correlation in savings outcomes (standard errors clustered on the individual; pre/post collapse in Table A1 column 1)
endogeneity of lagged housing wealth (Table A1 column 4)
robustness_checks: placebo reforms in 2008, 2007, 2006 and 2005 (Table 2, row 1)
donut-hole excluding individuals with 2008 annuity contributions of DKK 90,000-110,000 (Table 2, row 2)
varying the treatment assignment window above the DKK 100,000-threshold (Fig. 5)
collapsing pre- and post-reform years (Table A1 column 1)
including pre-reform self-employed individuals and their spouses (Table A1 column 2)
normalising outcome variables by lagged income (Table A1 column 3)
omitting lagged housing wealth (Table A1 column 4)
restricting to individuals who did not change address after 2010 (Table A4 column 1)
measuring the post-reform response in 2010, 2010-2011 and 2010-2012 (Table A4 columns 2-4)
adding geographical region x year, educational level x year and tax-bracket x year interactions (Table 1 columns 2-4)
estimating Eqs. (1)-(3) by OLS (results not reported)
conditioning on consecutive pre-reform years of treatment/control-size contributions (Table A2 and online appendix)
loan-to-income instead of loan-to-value subgroups (Fig. B6)
unresolved_confounders: price changes cannot be separated from quantity changes because the flow variables are calculated as year-on-year changes in stock variables

estimator.value: 2SLS (two-step difference-in-differences with Treat_i x Post_i,t as instrument)

ambiguities: Table 1 prints positive values under the heading 'Crowding-out when reducing annuity pensions by 1 unit', while gamma in Eqs. (2)-(3) is the coefficient on annuity pension contributions; the sign convention linking the printed numbers to gamma is not stated explicitly, so the treatment is recorded here as a DKK 1 REDUCTION.
The horizon 0-3 years is derived from the reform year 2010 and the sample end 2013; the paper states only that Post_i,t equals 1 in all post-reform years.

evidence.annotation: Fig. 3. Annuity pension contributions. Note: Average contributions for annuity schemes are calculated within each year for the treated and non-treated groups. For each group, contributions are then indexed to 100 in 2009.
Fig. 4. Alternative saving accounts. Note: See Fig. 3.

Fig. 2. Histogram of annuity pension contributions. Note: Individuals are grouped in equal sized bins by annuity pension contributions. The darker bars represent the distribution immediately before the reform was implemented, while the lighter bars represent the distribution of pension contributions in 2010.

evidence.how: The printed coefficient carries three asterisks and the table note defines ***, ** and * as the 1%, 5% and 10% significance levels, so p < 0.01. The exact p-value is not printed.

value.as_printed: Z_{i,t} = alpha_i + Omega_t + Treat_i + gamma P-hat_{i,t} + X_{i,t-2} + r_{i,t}
value.lhs: Z_{i,t} (either life-long or capital pension contributions)
value.normalisation: Post_{i,t} takes the value 1 in all years after implementation of the reform (2010 and onwards), so the pre-reform years 2003-2009 are the omitted base period; Treat_i = 1 for individuals with 2008 annuity pension contributions above the DKK 100,000-threshold. P-hat_{i,t} is annuity pension contributions instrumented by Treat_i x Post_{i,t}; Table 1 prints the response to a 1 unit (DKK 1) reduction in annuity pension contributions.

value.claimed_domain: Savers in the upper half of the Danish income distribution (estimation-sample mean gross income about DKK 670,000), and specifically the introduction of a tax subsidy ceiling on pension contributions.
boundary_conditions: findings cannot necessarily be extrapolated directly to the broader population
results are specific to the introduction of a tax subsidy ceiling and do not speak to its removal or to an increase in tax incentives

Table 1 prints the change in each alternative account per 1 unit REDUCTION in annuity pension contributions, so a positive printed value means the account grows when annuity contributions fall.

timing.value: Measured annually; the reform was implemented in 2010 and Post_i,t equals 1 in all years after implementation.

register_source.value: Danish tax authorities' third-party reported annual information, merged at Statistics Denmark; no DST register code is named in the paper.

definition.value: Annual savings in financial assets, calculated as year-on-year changes in the stock of financial assets, in DKK after taxes; censored at the 1st and 99th percentile; the dependent variable S_i,t of Eq. (3).

timing.value: Annual flow, measured over the post-reform years (Post_i,t = 1 in all years after implementation of the reform in 2010); the panel runs 2003-2013 and mortgage information 2009-2013.

magnitude.interpretation: 4 cents was shifted to financial assets, statistically insignificant

key_assumptions.assumption: Instrument relevance: Treat_i x Post_i,t is strongly correlated with annuity pension contributions.

key_assumptions.assumption: Exclusion restriction: Treat_i x Post_i,t affects the savings outcome only through annuity pension contributions and is not correlated with some common third factor.

key_assumptions.assumption: No mean reversion: the measured reduction in annuity pension contributions is not a mechanical consequence of assigning groups on a single year's contributions.

population.description: Individuals residing in Denmark with annuity pension contributions of DKK 80,000-150,000 in 2008; self-employed individuals and their spouses excluded, individuals aged 60 or above excluded, and people not fully liable to taxation in Denmark excluded. 56,372 individuals, 599,744 person-year observations, 2003-2013.
population.ages: below 60 (individuals aged 60 or above are excluded); estimation-sample mean age 43.3
subgroups_defined: treated: annuity pension contributions of DKK 100,001-150,000 in 2008
non-treated: annuity pension contributions of DKK 80,000-100,000 in 2008
population.selection: Groups are assigned on 2008 annuity pension contributions, one year prior to the reform announcement; the estimation sample is explicitly not representative of the full Danish population and covers savers in the upper part of the income distribution (estimation-sample mean gross income DKK 668,500 against DKK 305,200 in the full sample).

identification.source_of_variation: The Danish 2010 tax reform, which made employer-paid plus individual contributions to annuity pension schemes tax-deductible only up to DKK 100,000, here replaced by a placebo reform in 2008, a year with no reform.

key_assumptions.assumption: Parallel pre-trends: treated and non-treated groups exhibited common trends in annuity pension contributions prior to the reform.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Fig. 3: indexed group means of annuity pension contributions, 2003-2013

key_assumptions.assumption: Treat_i x Post_i,t is not correlated with the idiosyncratic error term, conditional on individual and year fixed effects and lagged controls.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Graphical inspection of pre-reform annuity pension contributions (Fig. 3)

rhs: epsilon_i,t (idiosyncratic error in annuity pension contributions)

key_assumptions.assumption: No anticipation: individuals did not adjust annuity pension contributions before the reform was implemented.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Fig. 2: smooth pre-reform histogram around the DKK 100,000-threshold

implies_edges.to: annuity pension contributions in pre-reform years

key_assumptions.assumption: No self-selection into the groups: assignment uses 2008 annuity pension contributions, one year before the reform was announced.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Timing of the assignment rule

key_assumptions.assumption: No mean reversion in annuity pension contributions across years.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Placebo reforms in 2008, 2007, 2006 and 2005 and the donut-hole test (Table 2)

key_assumptions.assumption: Inherent savings propensities are approximately constant over the observation period.

threats_discussed: mean reversion in annuity pension contributions (tested with placebo reforms, Table 2)
sensitivity to the assignment window around the DKK 100,000-threshold (Fig. 5)
misallocation into the control group of individuals who behave like treated individuals (Table A2)
individuals forced to move out of their homes after 2010 (non-mover subsample, Table A4 column 1)
differential housing wealth and income trends between the groups (Figs. B4a and B4b)
differential exposure to unemployment and labour supply responses (Figs. B5a and B5b)
other elements of the 2010 tax reform: removal of the middle tax bracket and increase of the top tax bracket (Table 1 columns 3-4)
serial correlation in savings outcomes (standard errors clustered on the individual; pre/post collapse in Table A1 column 1)
endogeneity of lagged housing wealth (Table A1 column 4)
robustness_checks: placebo reforms in 2008, 2007, 2006 and 2005 (Table 2, row 1)
donut-hole excluding individuals with 2008 annuity contributions of DKK 90,000-110,000 (Table 2, row 2)
varying the treatment assignment window above the DKK 100,000-threshold (Fig. 5)
collapsing pre- and post-reform years (Table A1 column 1)
including pre-reform self-employed individuals and their spouses (Table A1 column 2)
normalising outcome variables by lagged income (Table A1 column 3)
omitting lagged housing wealth (Table A1 column 4)
restricting to individuals who did not change address after 2010 (Table A4 column 1)
measuring the post-reform response in 2010, 2010-2011 and 2010-2012 (Table A4 columns 2-4)
adding geographical region x year, educational level x year and tax-bracket x year interactions (Table 1 columns 2-4)
estimating Eqs. (1)-(3) by OLS (results not reported)
conditioning on consecutive pre-reform years of treatment/control-size contributions (Table A2 and online appendix)
loan-to-income instead of loan-to-value subgroups (Fig. B6)
unresolved_confounders: price changes cannot be separated from quantity changes because the flow variables are calculated as year-on-year changes in stock variables

estimator.value: OLS difference-in-differences with two-way fixed effects (Eq. (1))

dummy for being divorced within 2 years (t-2)

ambiguities: The paper states only that the placebo setup is 'shifted backwards in time such that saving responses are measured in' the placebo year; it does not say whether Post equals 1 in that year only or in that year and onwards, so no numeric horizon is recorded.

The baseline mean and SD are taken from the 'Pension contributions' row of the summary statistics (Table A3, estimation sample, pre-reform years 2003-2009, DKK 1,000); that row is not explicitly restricted to annuity pension contributions.

evidence.annotation: Fig. 3. Annuity pension contributions. Note: Average contributions for annuity schemes are calculated within each year for the treated and non-treated groups. For each group, contributions are then indexed to 100 in 2009.

Fig. 2. Histogram of annuity pension contributions. Note: Individuals are grouped in equal sized bins by annuity pension contributions. The darker bars represent the distribution immediately before the reform was implemented, while the lighter bars represent the distribution of pension contributions in 2010.

evidence.how: Table A3 reports a mean of 96.5 and a standard deviation of 89.9 for 'Pension contributions' in the estimation sample, in units of DKK 1,000 and over the pre-reform years 2003-2009; multiplied by 1,000 this is DKK 96,500 (SD DKK 89,900). The row is labelled 'Pension contributions' rather than annuity contributions specifically.

target_designation.reasoning: Eq. (1): 'The parameter of interest is delta as it measures the nominal change in annuity pension contributions for the treated relative to the non-treated group in the post-reform period.'

anchor_quote.text: Estimates of the placebo reforms are close to zero except for the 2005 parameter, which is significant with DKK 1,280.

claims.statement: A placebo reform in 2007, a year unaffected by the actual reform, did not significantly change annuity pension contributions of the assigned treatment group by DKK 103.

treatment.label: Treat_i x Post_i,t (exposure to the placebo reform year 2007, in place of the 2010 DKK 100,000 annuity deduction ceiling)

value.as_printed: S_{i,t} = alpha_i + Omega_t + Treat_i + gamma P-hat_{i,t}(1 - tau_i) + X_{i,t-2} + r_{i,t}
value.lhs: S_{i,t} (mortgage debt repayments, bank debt repayments, bank deposits or savings in financial assets)
value.normalisation: Post_{i,t} takes the value 1 in all years after implementation of the reform (2010 and onwards), so the pre-reform years 2003-2009 are the omitted base period; Treat_i = 1 for individuals with 2008 annuity pension contributions above the DKK 100,000-threshold. Annuity pension contributions enter after taxes as P-hat_{i,t}(1 - tau_i), with the mean tax rate tau_i fixed at its 2008 level; Table 1 prints the response to a 1 unit (DKK 1) reduction in annuity pension contributions.

definition.value: A 1 unit (DKK 1) reduction in annual individual contributions to annuity pension schemes, P_i,t, induced by the Danish 2010 tax reform that capped the tax deduction for annuity pension contributions at DKK 100,000. In Eqs. (2) and (3) annuity pension contributions are instrumented by Treat_i x Post_i,t; in Eq. (3) they enter after taxes as P_i,t(1-tau_i) with the mean tax rate tau_i fixed at its 2008 level. Table 1 prints the change in each alternative account per 1 unit REDUCTION in annuity pension contributions, so a positive printed value means the account grows when annuity contributions fall.

estimand.target_population: Treated 30-44 year-olds who changed annuity pension contributions because of the reform.
estimand.compliers: Savers in this subgroup who reduced annuity pension contributions in response to the DKK 100,000 deduction ceiling.
estimand.time_horizon: All post-reform years: Post_i,t takes the value 1 in all years after implementation of the reform (2010-2013).

population.description: Individuals residing in Denmark with annuity pension contributions of DKK 80,000-150,000 in 2008; self-employed individuals and their spouses excluded, individuals aged 60 or above excluded, and people not fully liable to taxation in Denmark excluded. 56,372 individuals, 599,744 person-year observations, 2003-2013. Estimated separately on subgroups defined by 5-year age intervals.
population.ages: below 60 (individuals aged 60 or above are excluded); estimation-sample mean age 43.3
subgroups_defined: treated: annuity pension contributions of DKK 100,001-150,000 in 2008
non-treated: annuity pension contributions of DKK 80,000-100,000 in 2008
5-year age intervals spanning ages 30-59
population.selection: Groups are assigned on 2008 annuity pension contributions, one year prior to the reform announcement; the estimation sample is explicitly not representative of the full Danish population and covers savers in the upper part of the income distribution (estimation-sample mean gross income DKK 668,500 against DKK 305,200 in the full sample).

identification.source_of_variation: The Danish 2010 tax reform, which made employer-paid plus individual contributions to annuity pension schemes tax-deductible only up to DKK 100,000; Eqs. (2) and (3) are estimated separately on each subgroup.

key_assumptions.assumption: Parallel pre-trends: the treated and non-treated groups would have had similar changes in the savings outcome had the reform not been implemented.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Graphical inspection of pre-reform group means in Figs. 3, 4a, 4b, B3 and B4

key_assumptions.assumption: Instrument relevance: Treat_i x Post_i,t is strongly correlated with annuity pension contributions.
key_assumptions.supported_by: First stage in Table 2 column 1: a DKK 21,038 reduction in annuity pension contributions, statistically significant with p < .001

key_assumptions.assumption: Exclusion restriction: Treat_i x Post_i,t affects the savings outcome only through annuity pension contributions and is not correlated with some common third factor.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Graphical inspection of pre-trends in the outcome variables

implies_edges.to: Mortgage debt repayments, 30-44 year-olds (annual flow, DKK)

key_assumptions.assumption: No anticipation: individuals did not adjust annuity pension contributions before the reform was implemented.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Fig. 2: the pre-reform histogram of annuity pension contributions is smooth around the DKK 100,000-threshold, while bunching appears only after implementation

implies_edges.to: annuity pension contributions in pre-reform years

key_assumptions.assumption: No self-selection into treatment: groups are assigned on 2008 annuity pension contributions, one year before the reform was announced.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Timing of the assignment rule

key_assumptions.assumption: No mean reversion: the measured reduction in annuity pension contributions is not a mechanical consequence of assigning groups on a single year's contributions.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Placebo reforms in 2008, 2007, 2006 and 2005 (Table 2) and the donut-hole test

key_assumptions.assumption: Inherent savings propensities are approximately constant over the observation period.
The price (substitution) channel dominates the wealth channel, so the comparison of treated and non-treated savers recovers the substitution effect.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Cites Duflo et al. (2006) and Engelhardt and Kumar (2007)

key_assumptions.assumption: Monotonicity of the response to the instrument, required for the 2SLS estimate to be a local average treatment effect.

threats_discussed: mean reversion in annuity pension contributions (tested with placebo reforms, Table 2)
sensitivity to the assignment window around the DKK 100,000-threshold (Fig. 5)
misallocation into the control group of individuals who behave like treated individuals (Table A2)
individuals forced to move out of their homes after 2010 (non-mover subsample, Table A4 column 1)
differential housing wealth and income trends between the groups (Figs. B4a and B4b)
differential exposure to unemployment and labour supply responses (Figs. B5a and B5b)
other elements of the 2010 tax reform: removal of the middle tax bracket and increase of the top tax bracket (Table 1 columns 3-4)
serial correlation in savings outcomes (standard errors clustered on the individual; pre/post collapse in Table A1 column 1)
endogeneity of lagged housing wealth (Table A1 column 4)
robustness_checks: placebo reforms in 2008, 2007, 2006 and 2005 (Table 2, row 1)
donut-hole excluding individuals with 2008 annuity contributions of DKK 90,000-110,000 (Table 2, row 2)
varying the treatment assignment window above the DKK 100,000-threshold (Fig. 5)
collapsing pre- and post-reform years (Table A1 column 1)
including pre-reform self-employed individuals and their spouses (Table A1 column 2)
normalising outcome variables by lagged income (Table A1 column 3)
omitting lagged housing wealth (Table A1 column 4)
restricting to individuals who did not change address after 2010 (Table A4 column 1)
measuring the post-reform response in 2010, 2010-2011 and 2010-2012 (Table A4 columns 2-4)
adding geographical region x year, educational level x year and tax-bracket x year interactions (Table 1 columns 2-4)
estimating Eqs. (1)-(3) by OLS (results not reported)
conditioning on consecutive pre-reform years of treatment/control-size contributions (Table A2 and online appendix)
loan-to-income instead of loan-to-value subgroups (Fig. B6)
unresolved_confounders: price changes cannot be separated from quantity changes because the flow variables are calculated as year-on-year changes in stock variables

estimator.value: 2SLS (Eqs. (2) and (3)) estimated separately on each subgroup
